title: Preventing Siphonage in Drain Traps
description: A P-trap relies on a standing water seal to block sewer gases from entering living spaces. However, if the trap arm is not properly vented or if an improper trap configuration is used, the velocity of draining water creates a negative pressure vacuum. This siphon action can suck standing water completely out of the trap, leaving the seal depleted. To maintain a functional liquid seal, ensure the trap arm is correctly vented according to local piping design standards before transitioning to the drain stack, protecting indoor air quality.

Preventing Siphonage in Drain Traps

A P-trap relies on a standing water seal to block sewer gases from entering living spaces. However, if the trap arm is not properly vented or if an improper trap configuration is used, the velocity of draining water creates a negative pressure vacuum. This siphon action can suck standing water completely out of the trap, leaving the seal depleted. To maintain a functional liquid seal, ensure the trap arm is correctly vented according to local piping design standards before transitioning to the drain stack, protecting indoor air quality.
